cards.definition: **Definition.** A decidable condition tied to an identified artifact and observation that would support one clause of the requested change.
major_error_concepts: Saying duplicates are handled correctly without an observable result denominator or unchanged-state check.
cards.prompt: Define Acceptance criterion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A decidable condition tied to an identified artifact and observation that would support one clause of the requested change.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The complete list of code interfaces tests docs configuration generated artifacts persisted state callers and workflows that may observe the change.
major_error_concepts: Editing only the visible command function while a wrapper still maps every exception to success.
cards.prompt: Define Affected-surface inventory. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The complete list of code interfaces tests docs configuration generated artifacts persisted state callers and workflows that may observe the change.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The requirement that tests reviews and artifacts refer to the exact current content rather than a parent or pre-mutation version.
major_error_concepts: Treating branch name or pull-request identity as proof that prior evidence covers changed bytes.
cards.prompt: Define Change-evidence freshness. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The requirement that tests reviews and artifacts refer to the exact current content rather than a parent or pre-mutation version.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The line and artifact level comparison between requested surfaces actual patch generated changes and unrelated user work.
major_error_concepts: Reviewing the aggregate patch as one change because all modifications were produced by one command.
cards.prompt: Define Change-scope reconciliation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The line and artifact level comparison between requested surfaces actual patch generated changes and unrelated user work.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The precommitted condition that pauses implementation or promotion when scope identity evidence or safety assumptions no longer match the release.
major_error_concepts: Continuing because the extra change seems small while the acceptance and rollback contracts are now stale.
cards.prompt: Define Change stop rule. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The precommitted condition that pauses implementation or promotion when scope identity evidence or safety assumptions no longer match the release.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The row-complete mapping from each acceptance risk compatibility and nonclaim clause to its required test inspection artifact and owner.
major_error_concepts: Listing many tests without identifying which claim each one supports or which clause remains untested.
cards.prompt: Define Evidence-obligation matrix. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The row-complete mapping from each acceptance risk compatibility and nonclaim clause to its required test inspection artifact and owner.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A nearby behavior intentionally excluded from the specified change so reviewers can detect accidental scope expansion.
major_error_concepts: Performing a broad validation cleanup and calling it necessary without dependency evidence.
cards.prompt: Define Explicit non-goal. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A nearby behavior intentionally excluded from the specified change so reviewers can detect accidental scope expansion.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The separation among locally reachable commits locally cached remote-tracking references and current server state.
major_error_concepts: Calling a clean or locally synchronized status proof that no remote commit or review update exists.
cards.prompt: Define Local-history and remote-state distinction. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The separation among locally reachable commits locally cached remote-tracking references and current server state.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The evidence-backed separation between what the current version actually does what the request asks and what the author assumes it should do.
major_error_concepts: Restating the report as fact without reproducing the exact version configuration and input.
cards.prompt: Define Observed-versus-requested behavior. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The evidence-backed separation between what the current version actually does what the request asks and what the author assumes it should do.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The versioned set of relevant tests reproductions warnings measurements and known failures captured before implementation.
major_error_concepts: Reporting only the post-change run and attributing every failure or pass to the patch.
cards.prompt: Define Prechange baseline. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The versioned set of relevant tests reproductions warnings measurements and known failures captured before implementation.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The exact repository worktree branch head commit remotes and relevant submodule or generated-state identity on which change evidence is formed.
major_error_concepts: Reporting a green baseline without enough repository identity to distinguish another worktree or later commit.
cards.prompt: Define Repository identity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The exact repository worktree branch head commit remotes and relevant submodule or generated-state identity on which change evidence is formed.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A falsifiable statement connecting one proposed change mechanism to a plausible failure impact and decisive check.
major_error_concepts: Writing high risk in a review description without a mechanism impact or test.
cards.prompt: Define Risk hypothesis. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A falsifiable statement connecting one proposed change mechanism to a plausible failure impact and decisive check.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Staging-index state is the proposed next snapshot held separately from HEAD and the working tree; staged changes are index-versus-HEAD differences and may not match current filesystem content.
major_error_concepts: Treating the index as a list of filenames rather than content selected for the next snapshot.
cards.prompt: Define Staging-index state. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The staging index holds the proposed next snapshot separately from HEAD.
The staging index holds the proposed next snapshot separately from the working tree.
A staged change is a difference between the index and HEAD.
The content staged in the index may differ from the file's current working-tree content.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The named people programs interfaces operators and downstream artifacts whose behavior or evidence may be changed by the work.
major_error_concepts: Calling the requester the only stakeholder while silently changing machine callers and stored artifacts.
cards.prompt: Define Stakeholder and consumer identity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The named people programs interfaces operators and downstream artifacts whose behavior or evidence may be changed by the work.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The status-diff-log evidence triad compares HEAD, index, and working tree state, inspects their content deltas, and relates them to commit-history topology before mutation.
major_error_concepts: Using one command output as a complete repository audit despite its deliberately narrower view.
cards.prompt: Define Status-diff-log evidence triad. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Status evidence compares the states of HEAD, the staging index, and the working tree.
Diff evidence inspects the content deltas among the relevant repository states.
Log evidence relates the inspected state to commit-history topology.
The status-diff-log triad is read before a repository mutation so the mutation starts from an identified state.

accepted_variants: A new file becomes tracked when staged even before its first commit. Ignore rules filter untracked candidates; adding a pattern does not untrack existing content or make it secret.
cards.definition: Tracked status is about files Git already tracks through its snapshot/index state, including newly staged files; prior commit history is not required. Untracked files are not represented by that tracking state. Ignore rules normally suppress matching untracked candidates from ordinary discovery; they do not untrack an already tracked file or guarantee confidentiality.
major_error_concepts: A file cannot be tracked until committed once, and adding it to .gitignore removes it from tracking.
cards.prompt: Distinguish tracked, untracked and ignored files in Git. Can a never-committed file already be tracked, and does an ignore pattern untrack existing tracked content?
required_concepts: Include newly staged never-committed files among tracked files; untracked means not currently represented by Git's tracking state.
Ignore matching does not remove an already tracked file from version control and is not a secrecy guarantee.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Working-tree state is the checked-out filesystem content and metadata visible to Git, distinct from both the HEAD commit and the staging index; unstaged changes are worktree-versus-index differences.
major_error_concepts: Calling the file staged and assuming all current contents will enter the next commit.
cards.prompt: Define Working-tree state. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Working-tree state is the checked-out filesystem content and metadata visible to Git.
Working-tree state is distinct from the snapshot named by HEAD.
Working-tree state is distinct from the staging index.
An unstaged change is a difference between the working tree and the staging index.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A reviewable history node with one purpose complete enough to validate and free of unrelated cleanup or generated noise.
major_error_concepts: Equating atomic with one file or combining unrelated fixes because they were discovered in one session.
cards.prompt: Define Atomic cohesive commit. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A reviewable history node with one purpose complete enough to validate and free of unrelated cleanup or generated noise.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A movable named reference to a commit rather than a copied directory or permanent line of development.
major_error_concepts: Treating a branch as containing commits exclusively when commits can be reachable from many references.
cards.prompt: Define Branch reference. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A movable named reference to a commit rather than a copied directory or permanent line of development.

accepted_variants: It replays the selected change. Usually that records a new commit, but --ff can move HEAD to the existing commit when HEAD is its parent; --no-commit changes the index/worktree without committing.
cards.definition: Cherry-pick applies the change introduced by a selected commit relative to its parent (or chosen mainline for a merge) onto the current context. Normal replay records a new commit, commonly with a new parent/identity. With --ff and HEAD equal to the selected commit's parent, Git advances to the existing commit. --no-commit applies changes to the index and working tree without creating a commit. Application may require conflict resolution.
major_error_concepts: Every successful cherry-pick necessarily creates a distinct commit object, including --ff and --no-commit.
cards.prompt: What change does cherry-pick replay, and does every invocation create a distinct commit? Explain the --ff and --no-commit cases.
required_concepts: Describe replaying the selected commit's change into the current context.
Qualify new-commit behavior: eligible --ff preserves the existing commit identity; --no-commit makes no commit.

accepted_variants: It records a tree snapshot, author/committer metadata, message and parent references. Root commits have none, ordinary commits one, and merges two or more; it is not merely a diff.
cards.definition: A commit object records a tree snapshot reference, author and committer metadata, message and zero or more parent commit references. A root commit has zero parents, an ordinary non-root commit normally has one, and a merge commit has two or more. The object is content-addressed and immutable; its recorded tree is not merely a stored diff.
major_error_concepts: Every valid commit must have at least one parent; a parentless root is malformed.
cards.prompt: What does a Git commit object record, and how many parents can root, ordinary and merge commits have?
required_concepts: Identify the snapshot/tree reference, metadata/message and parent references as commit content.
State root=0 parents, ordinary non-root=1, merge>=2.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The directed relation encoding which earlier commit or commits a commit continues and therefore its history topology.
major_error_concepts: Inferring parentage from timestamp order or branch labels instead of object links.
cards.prompt: Define Commit parentage. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The directed relation encoding which earlier commit or commits a commit continues and therefore its history topology.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A Git commit identifier hashes the serialized commit object, including its tree, parent identifiers, author and committer metadata, and message, so equal file trees can still have different commit identities and histories.
major_error_concepts: Treating a Git commit identifier as only a hash of working-tree files or assuming equal trees imply equal commits.
cards.prompt: Define Git commit content-addressed identity.
required_concepts: A Git commit identifier hashes the serialized commit object.
The serialized commit object includes the commit's tree identifier.
The serialized commit object includes its parent commit identifiers.
The serialized commit object includes author and committer metadata.
The serialized commit object includes the commit message.
Two commits with equal file trees can still have different commit identifiers and different histories.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The movement of a target reference to a descendant when no divergent target commits require a new merge node.
major_error_concepts: Calling every branch integration a merge commit or losing that no new snapshot is computed here.
cards.prompt: Define Fast-forward integration. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The movement of a target reference to a descendant when no divergent target commits require a new merge node.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The bounded search over an ordered ancestry using a reliable good bad classifier to identify the first change correlated with a regression.
major_error_concepts: Running a flaky test as an oracle and naming the final commit causal without inspecting the introduced change.
cards.prompt: Define History-bisection contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The bounded search over an ordered ancestry using a reliable good bad classifier to identify the first change correlated with a regression.

accepted_variants: It is a common ancestor with no strictly newer-in-ancestry common descendant. Several incomparable best ancestors can exist, so timestamps do not select a universally unique base.
cards.definition: A merge base is a best common ancestor: there is no other common ancestor that is a strict descendant of it. This is a graph-ancestry condition, not a timestamp rule. In criss-cross histories there may be several incomparable best common ancestors, so not every pair has one unique merge base.
major_error_concepts: Any selected common ancestor is a merge base, and the one with the latest timestamp is always the unique correct choice.
cards.prompt: Define a Git merge base for two commits. What makes a common ancestor 'best', and can there be more than one?
required_concepts: Require common ancestry plus absence of a strictly better descendant common ancestor.
Allow multiple incomparable best common ancestors; do not choose solely by timestamp.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The condition where automatic integration cannot choose one result under its textual or structural rules and requires an explicit resolution.
major_error_concepts: Choosing ours or theirs solely to remove markers while discarding the other required behavior.
cards.prompt: Define Merge conflict. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The condition where automatic integration cannot choose one result under its textual or structural rules and requires an explicit resolution.

accepted_variants: Parent links find ancestor commits. General object traversal also follows tags to targets, commits to trees and trees to subtrees/blobs; a root still reaches its files.
cards.definition: Commit ancestry follows parent links from selected commits/references. General object reachability also follows annotated tags to their targets, commits to their trees, and trees to contained subtrees/blobs. Therefore a root commit can reach its tree and files despite having no parent. Removing one reference does not alone prove objects are unreachable or immediately collected.
major_error_concepts: All reachable objects can be found by parent links alone, so a root commit reaches no tree or blob.
cards.prompt: Distinguish Git commit reachability from general object reachability. Are parent links alone enough to determine all reachable objects?
required_concepts: Use parent links for commit ancestry.
For general objects, include tag-target, commit-tree and tree-entry links; parent links alone are insufficient.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The construction of new commits by replaying selected changes on a different base thereby changing commit identities and topology.
major_error_concepts: Saying rebase moves existing commits unchanged or is safe on shared history regardless of collaborators.
cards.prompt: Define Rebase replay. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The construction of new commits by replaying selected changes on a different base thereby changing commit identities and topology.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The local reference-update journal that can locate recently displaced commit identities within its retention boundary.
major_error_concepts: Assuming reflog is permanent remote shared or guaranteed after expiry and garbage collection.
cards.prompt: Define Reflog recovery. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The local reference-update journal that can locate recently displaced commit identities within its retention boundary.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The separate movement of references index and working-tree content whose modes can discard uncommitted or reachable state.
major_error_concepts: Using reset restore and checkout from memory without modeling which state stores will change.
cards.prompt: Define Reset and restore boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The separate movement of references index and working-tree content whose modes can discard uncommitted or reachable state.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A new history node whose change inversely applies an earlier change while retaining the original and subsequent history.
major_error_concepts: Resetting the shared branch backward and calling the prior release never happened.
cards.prompt: Define Revert commit. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A new history node whose change inversely applies an earlier change while retaining the original and subsequent history.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The search for behaviorally incompatible changes even when an integration tool reports no textual conflict.
major_error_concepts: Treating automatic merge success as evidence the combined program is correct.
cards.prompt: Define Semantic-conflict validation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The search for behaviorally incompatible changes even when an integration tool reports no textual conflict.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The collaboration rule that rewriting commits others may reference invalidates their topology and can duplicate or lose work during reconciliation.
major_error_concepts: Treating force-with-lease as proof that no collaborator or automation relies on the old history.
cards.prompt: Define Shared-history rewrite boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The collaboration rule that rewriting commits others may reference invalidates their topology and can duplicate or lose work during reconciliation.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The integration of two descendant changes relative to a merge base into a result snapshot commonly recorded with both tips as parents.
major_error_concepts: Concatenating tip diffs without considering shared base renames deletions or interacting semantics.
cards.prompt: Define Three-way merge. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The integration of two descendant changes relative to a merge base into a result snapshot commonly recorded with both tips as parents.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The search for reachable symbols output fields exception text files ordering or timing that consumers use despite weak intentionality and whose change carries real risk.
major_error_concepts: Declaring undocumented means unused or permanently supported without evidence.
cards.prompt: Define Accidental-public-API diagnostic. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: An accidental-public-API diagnostic searches for reachable symbols that consumers use despite weak intentionality.
The diagnostic searches for output fields that consumers rely on despite weak intentionality.
The diagnostic searches for exception text that consumers rely on despite weak intentionality.
The diagnostic searches for files that consumers rely on despite weak intentionality.
The diagnostic searches for observable ordering that consumers rely on despite weak intentionality.
The diagnostic searches for observable timing that consumers rely on despite weak intentionality.
Changing an observed surface used by consumers carries compatibility risk even when that surface was not intentionally declared public.

cards.definition: **Definition.** An interface extension that preserves all established consumer behaviors while introducing optional new capability under the specified compatibility policy.
major_error_concepts: Calling any added field compatible when strict decoders reject unknown fields or positional callers change binding.
cards.prompt: Define Additive-compatible change. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: An interface extension that preserves all established consumer behaviors while introducing optional new capability under the specified compatibility policy.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The requirement that a substituting implementation accept the promised inputs preserve outputs invariants and error or side-effect expectations without strengthening caller duties.
major_error_concepts: Using shared method names or inheritance syntax as proof of behavioral compatibility.
cards.prompt: Define Behavioral subtyping contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A behavioral subtype accepts every input promised by the substituted interface.
A behavioral subtype preserves the promised outputs.
A behavioral subtype preserves the interface invariants.
A behavioral subtype preserves the promised error behavior.
A behavioral subtype preserves the promised side-effect behavior.
A behavioral subtype does not strengthen the duties imposed on callers.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A change that invalidates a previously conforming caller observation data contract or operational assumption under the declared stability policy.
major_error_concepts: Classifying from implementation diff size rather than consumer-validity change.
cards.prompt: Define Breaking interface change. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A change that invalidates a previously conforming caller observation data contract or operational assumption under the declared stability policy.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The predicate required for every externally observable stable state of an object across all public operations.
major_error_concepts: Checking the invariant only at initialization while later mutation can violate it.
cards.prompt: Define Class invariant. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The predicate required for every externally observable stable state of an object across all public operations.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The explicit producer consumer version and behavior grid showing which combinations are supported tested deprecated or rejected.
major_error_concepts: Testing only the newest pair and inferring mixed-version compatibility.
cards.prompt: Define Compatibility matrix. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The explicit producer consumer version and behavior grid showing which combinations are supported tested deprecated or rejected.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A behavior change that restores the declared contract without breaking consumers that legitimately relied on allowed behavior.
major_error_concepts: Treating every changed output as breaking or every bug fix as automatically harmless to all real consumers.
cards.prompt: Define Compatible defect repair. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A behavior change that restores the declared contract without breaking consumers that legitimately relied on allowed behavior.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The ordered changes compatibility bridge validation communication and rollback route moving consumers from one contract to another.
major_error_concepts: Changing all known repository references while external or persisted consumers remain unidentified.
cards.prompt: Define Consumer migration plan. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The ordered changes compatibility bridge validation communication and rollback route moving consumers from one contract to another.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The executable examples checking selected observable promises at a consumer boundary without proving every behavior or implementation invariant.
major_error_concepts: Mocking the implementation internals so the test passes even when the public wiring is broken.
cards.prompt: Define Contract-test boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The executable examples checking selected observable promises at a consumer boundary without proving every behavior or implementation invariant.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The announced continued-support interval warning mechanism replacement path measurement and removal gate for a public behavior.
major_error_concepts: Logging a warning once and removing the flag without proving consumers migrated.
cards.prompt: Define Deprecation contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The announced continued-support interval warning mechanism replacement path measurement and removal gate for a public behavior.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The declared failure classes representation state effects retry meaning and diagnostic stability available to callers.
major_error_concepts: Throwing an arbitrary internal exception after mutation and expecting callers to parse prose.
cards.prompt: Define Error contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The declared failure classes representation state effects retry meaning and diagnostic stability available to callers.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The versioned expected serialization or output used to detect changes whose update requires semantic review rather than blind regeneration.
major_error_concepts: Updating all snapshots because tests failed and erasing evidence of an accidental breaking change.
cards.prompt: Define Golden-artifact contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The versioned expected serialization or output used to detect changes whose update requires semantic review rather than blind regeneration.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The declared set of callable operations accepted inputs returned outputs errors side effects state transitions timing or ordering promises and stability status visible to consumers.
major_error_concepts: Listing a function signature while leaving errors mutation ordering and compatibility unspecified.
cards.prompt: Define Interface contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: An interface contract declares the callable operations visible to consumers.
An interface contract declares the accepted inputs for those operations.
An interface contract declares the returned outputs.
An interface contract declares the errors consumers may observe.
An interface contract declares the side effects consumers may observe.
An interface contract declares the state transitions consumers may observe.
An interface contract declares any timing promises visible to consumers.
An interface contract declares any ordering promises visible to consumers.
An interface contract declares the stability status of each promised surface.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The durable context alternatives contract compatibility impact migration consequences and owner for a consequential interface choice.
major_error_concepts: Writing a decision title with no rejected alternatives consequences or supersession rule.
cards.prompt: Define Interface-decision record. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The durable context alternatives contract compatibility impact migration consequences and owner for a consequential interface choice.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The provider guarantee portion of a public contract whose outputs state changes and errors must remain valid for conforming consumers across versions.
major_error_concepts: Saying success means no exception without describing the resulting externally visible state or compatibility impact.
cards.prompt: Define Interface postcondition evolution. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The provider guarantee portion of a public contract whose outputs state changes and errors must remain valid for conforming consumers across versions.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The caller obligation portion of a public contract whose strengthening weakening validation and migration impact must be judged across existing consumers.
major_error_concepts: Silently strengthening the caller obligation during cleanup and treating defensive rejection as compatible.
cards.prompt: Define Interface precondition evolution. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The caller obligation portion of a public contract whose strengthening weakening validation and migration impact must be judged across existing consumers.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The guarantee that implementations may change hidden representation while preserving all observed observations.
major_error_concepts: Calling it a refactor while deterministic iteration visible to clients changes.
cards.prompt: Define Internal representation independence. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The guarantee that implementations may change hidden representation while preserving all observed observations.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The explicit declaration of which symbols data shapes commands files behaviors and versions external consumers may depend on.
major_error_concepts: Calling every non-underscored implementation detail safe to change or every reachable symbol permanently public without policy.
cards.prompt: Define Public-interface boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The explicit declaration of which symbols data shapes commands files behaviors and versions external consumers may depend on.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The observable reads writes external calls ordering idempotence and atomicity associated with an operation.
major_error_concepts: Calling an operation read-only because its primary database is unchanged while it writes logs tokens or caches with semantic effects.
cards.prompt: Define Side-effect and state-transition contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The observable reads writes external calls ordering idempotence and atomicity associated with an operation.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The boundary across which consumers reason only from the specified contract while providers retain freedom to change conforming implementation.
major_error_concepts: Letting callers reach through the interface for one convenient internal operation and making the barrier nominal.
cards.prompt: Define Abstraction barrier. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The boundary across which consumers reason only from the specified contract while providers retain freedom to change conforming implementation.

cards.definition: **Definition.** An automated repository rule checking selected dependency or organization constraints without proving the architecture is optimal.
major_error_concepts: Treating a passing dependency linter as complete architectural evidence.
cards.prompt: Define Architecture fitness check boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: An automated repository rule checking selected dependency or organization constraints without proving the architecture is optimal.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The observed history of files components and owners that repeatedly change together used as evidence rather than proof of a better boundary.
major_error_concepts: Automatically merging files based on co-change counts without semantic or ownership review.
cards.prompt: Define Change-coupling profile. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The observed history of files components and owners that repeatedly change together used as evidence rather than proof of a better boundary.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The concrete compile runtime data temporal configuration or knowledge dependency through which one component constrains another.
major_error_concepts: Counting import statements only and missing shared schemas ordering assumptions or deployment coupling.
cards.prompt: Define Coupling relation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The concrete compile runtime data temporal configuration or knowledge dependency through which one component constrains another.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A directed path returning to its origin that can obstruct independent understanding construction testing ownership or release under the chosen dependency relation.
major_error_concepts: Calling all mutual runtime communication a source dependency cycle or resolving a cycle by moving files only.
cards.prompt: Define Dependency cycle. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A dependency cycle is a directed dependency path that returns to its origin.
Whether the path is a cycle is evaluated under one explicitly chosen dependency relation.
A dependency cycle can obstruct independent understanding of the participating components.
A dependency cycle can obstruct independent construction of the participating components.
A dependency cycle can obstruct independent testing of the participating components.
A dependency cycle can obstruct clear ownership of the participating components.
A dependency cycle can obstruct independent release of the participating components.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The directed graph whose nodes are components and edges name required interfaces data builds or runtime services under one declared relation.
major_error_concepts: Combining every relation into unlabeled arrows and diagnosing cycles that may not exist in any one graph.
cards.prompt: Define Dependency graph. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The directed graph whose nodes are components and edges name required interfaces data builds or runtime services under one declared relation.

cards.definition: **Definition.** An explicit boundary where control or data crosses through a consumer-shaped contract enabling substitution without exposing provider internals.
major_error_concepts: Creating an interface for every function even when there is no volatility test need or alternate provider.
cards.prompt: Define Dependency inversion seam. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: An explicit boundary where control or data crosses through a consumer-shaped contract enabling substitution without exposing provider internals.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The counts and identities of incoming consumers and outgoing dependencies qualified by contract stability and change impact.
major_error_concepts: Calling high fan-in good reuse or high fan-out bad complexity without inspecting relation quality.
cards.prompt: Define Fan-in and fan-out interpretation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The counts and identities of incoming consumers and outgoing dependencies qualified by contract stability and change impact.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The degree to which a component's elements jointly serve one stable responsibility and change for related reasons.
major_error_concepts: Maximizing file splitting without identifying stable responsibilities or common invariants.
cards.prompt: Define Functional cohesion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The degree to which a component's elements jointly serve one stable responsibility and change for related reasons.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The deliberate confinement of volatile representation and decision details behind a smaller stable interface.
major_error_concepts: Adding getters for every private field and claiming the representation is hidden.
cards.prompt: Define Information hiding. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The deliberate confinement of volatile representation and decision details behind a smaller stable interface.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The evidence-backed responsibility dependency alternatives migration compatibility owner and enforcement choice for a boundary change.
major_error_concepts: Drawing a preferred box diagram without code-level dependency or migration evidence.
cards.prompt: Define Module-boundary decision record. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The evidence-backed responsibility dependency alternatives migration compatibility owner and enforcement choice for a boundary change.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The coherent reason for a component to change together with its public boundary owned data invariants dependencies consumers and maintainer.
major_error_concepts: Calling every directory a module while responsibilities and invariant ownership cross its boundary arbitrarily.
cards.prompt: Define Module responsibility contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The coherent reason for a component to change together with its public boundary owned data invariants dependencies consumers and maintainer.

cards.definition: **Definition.** An executable check through a public boundary using controlled collaborators to validate behavior without binding to hidden representation.
major_error_concepts: Mocking every internal call so reorganization breaks tests despite unchanged behavior.
cards.prompt: Define Module seam test. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: An executable check through a public boundary using controlled collaborators to validate behavior without binding to hidden representation.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The deliberately exported minimal set of symbols and behaviors through which other packages depend on a module.
major_error_concepts: Treating import reachability as an intentional compatibility promise without review.
cards.prompt: Define Package public surface. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The deliberately exported minimal set of symbols and behaviors through which other packages depend on a module.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The arrangement of code around cohesive capabilities containing their nearby interface logic and tests while sharing only deliberate foundations.
major_error_concepts: Using feature folders to bypass common invariants and create incompatible local versions of core concepts.
cards.prompt: Define Repository organization by feature. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The arrangement of code around cohesive capabilities containing their nearby interface logic and tests while sharing only deliberate foundations.

accepted_variants: It groups presentation, application/domain and infrastructure roles under declared dependency rules. One feature can validly touch multiple layers; the coordination cost is a tradeoff, not automatic nonconformance.
cards.definition: Layered organization groups code by technical responsibilities and states which dependency directions/interfaces are allowed. A feature may legitimately span several layers; that can increase navigation and coordination costs without itself violating the architecture. Violations concern the chosen responsibility or dependency rules, not merely touching multiple layers.
major_error_concepts: Any feature that changes more than one layer proves the repository violates layered organization.
cards.prompt: Define repository organization by layer. Is a feature change touching presentation, application and persistence files automatically a violation of that organization?
required_concepts: Describe grouping by technical responsibility with explicit dependency rules.
Distinguish multi-layer feature-change tradeoffs from actual violations of those rules.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The small deliberately governed set of common concepts used by multiple features with strict compatibility and ownership to avoid a dumping ground.
major_error_concepts: Moving every helper to common and creating high-coupling ambiguous ownership.
cards.prompt: Define Shared-kernel boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The small deliberately governed set of common concepts used by multiple features with strict compatibility and ownership to avoid a dumping ground.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The policy that volatile or high-level components depend through stable abstractions rather than forcing stable policy to import volatile details.
major_error_concepts: Putting every interface in a generic folder while its ownership still follows the volatile implementation.
cards.prompt: Define Stable-dependency direction. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The policy that volatile or high-level components depend through stable abstractions rather than forcing stable policy to import volatile details.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The test for an interface wrapper or framework whose indirection cost lacks stable responsibility consumer need substitution evidence or volatility protection.
major_error_concepts: Keeping indirection because abstractions are always good or rejecting all one-use seams without volatility analysis.
cards.prompt: Define Unjustified-abstraction diagnostic. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The test for an interface wrapper or framework whose indirection cost lacks stable responsibility consumer need substitution evidence or volatility protection.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The equivalence of all declared observable outputs errors state effects ordering and resource promises across old and refactored implementations for the specified domain.
major_error_concepts: Checking only final values while warnings write ordering or exceptions changed.
cards.prompt: Define Behavior-preservation relation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A behavior-preserving refactoring keeps every declared observable output equivalent between the old and refactored implementations.
A behavior-preserving refactoring keeps every declared observable error equivalent.
A behavior-preserving refactoring keeps every declared observable state effect equivalent.
A behavior-preserving refactoring keeps every declared ordering promise equivalent.
A behavior-preserving refactoring keeps every declared resource promise equivalent.
Each equivalence claim is limited to the specified input and operating domain.

cards.definition: **Definition.** An executable observation of current behavior created before changing poorly understood code to detect unintentional drift without declaring every observed bug correct.
major_error_concepts: Treating a new characterization snapshot as normative specification or skipping decisive error and state cases.
cards.prompt: Define Characterization test. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A characterization test is an executable observation of current behavior.
A characterization test is created before changing code whose behavior is poorly understood.
A characterization test detects unintentional behavioral drift during the change.
A characterization test does not declare every observed bug to be correct behavior.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The count of independent control-flow paths used as a diagnostic that needs domain and test interpretation rather than an automatic defect verdict.
major_error_concepts: Using one threshold to prove poor design or splitting conditions until the metric falls while behavior becomes harder to follow.
cards.prompt: Define Cyclomatic-complexity boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The count of independent control-flow paths used as a diagnostic that needs domain and test interpretation rather than an automatic defect verdict.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The observed recurring cost defect risk review burden or delivery delay attributable to a debt item rather than imagined future harm.
major_error_concepts: Using story points or frustration alone as precise interest measurement.
cards.prompt: Define Debt-interest evidence. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The observed recurring cost defect risk review burden or delivery delay attributable to a debt item rather than imagined future harm.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The distinction among coincidental similarity repeated domain knowledge generated code and behavior that must change together.
major_error_concepts: Eliminating every similar line into a parameterized helper that couples unrelated concepts.
cards.prompt: Define Duplication classification. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The distinction among coincidental similarity repeated domain knowledge generated code and behavior that must change together.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The movement of a coherent operation behind a named boundary with inputs outputs errors and side effects made explicit.
major_error_concepts: Extracting code with many reference parameters and unchanged mixed responsibility then claiming modularity improved.
cards.prompt: Define Extract-function refactoring contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The movement of a coherent operation behind a named boundary with inputs outputs errors and side effects made explicit.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A test that passes despite missing the changed observable due to weak assertion shared implementation fixture or stale artifact.
major_error_concepts: Treating high test count or unchanged coverage percentage as behavior-equivalence proof.
cards.prompt: Define False-green refactor test. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A test that passes despite missing the changed observable due to weak assertion shared implementation fixture or stale artifact.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The search for multiple abstraction levels responsibilities state transitions or change drivers inside a large procedure rather than a line-count rule.
major_error_concepts: Extracting every five lines into methods whose names hide rather than clarify state flow.
cards.prompt: Define Long-method diagnostic. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The search for multiple abstraction levels responsibilities state transitions or change drivers inside a large procedure rather than a line-count rule.

accepted_variants: Relocate the behavior and invariants to the responsible module and preserve client behavior. An internal atomic caller update can be valid without an adapter; use a bridge when compatibility or rollout requires one.
cards.definition: It relocates behavior and associated invariant responsibility to a more appropriate module while preserving the declared client-visible behavior. Dependencies, callers and ownership must stay coherent. Staged adapters are useful when compatibility or rollout requires them, but an internal move can update all governed callers together without an adapter if no external contract changes.
major_error_concepts: A responsibility move is not a valid refactoring unless it always introduces staged adapters, even for a fully internal atomic change.
cards.prompt: What is move-responsibility refactoring, and are staged adapters required for every behavior-preserving move?
required_concepts: Move behavior and invariant responsibility while preserving declared client-visible semantics.
Treat adapters as conditional on compatibility/rollout needs, not universally mandatory.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The reader-task-specific evidence that names control flow invariants types comments and structure make intended behavior reconstructible without unnecessary inference.
major_error_concepts: Treating personal brevity preference or line count as an objective readability measure.
cards.prompt: Define Readability evidence. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Readability evidence is evaluated for a named reader task rather than as an unqualified property of code.
Readable names help the intended behavior be reconstructed.
Explicit control flow helps the intended behavior be reconstructed.
Stated invariants help the intended behavior be reconstructed.
Informative types help the intended behavior be reconstructed.
Relevant comments help the intended behavior be reconstructed.
Coherent structure helps the intended behavior be reconstructed.
The reconstruction should not require unnecessary inference from the reader.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The history and evidence discipline that isolates behavior-preserving transformations from intentional contract changes.
major_error_concepts: Calling the whole patch a refactor so reviewers overlook new failures or compatibility changes.
cards.prompt: Define Refactor-feature separation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The history and evidence discipline that isolates behavior-preserving transformations from intentional contract changes.

accepted_variants: A reproducible old/new difference violating the preservation contract is evidence tied to exact versions, input and environment. Isolate the change where possible; a larger valid witness still counts without global minimality.
cards.definition: Identify the old/new content, relevant input and environment, and a reproducible observable divergence that violates the claimed preservation relation. Isolate the responsible transformation as evidence permits. Shrinking a patch or input often improves diagnosis, but global minimality is not needed for a valid failure witness or a supported diagnosis.
major_error_concepts: A reproducible contract-breaking old/new difference is not diagnostic evidence until the failing input is proved globally smallest.
cards.prompt: What evidence supports a refactoring-regression diagnosis? Must the changed transformation or failing input be proved globally smallest?
required_concepts: Tie a reproducible old/new behavioral divergence to the preservation claim and identified change context.
Distinguish useful minimization from a mandatory global-smallest proof.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The update of a concept's identifier and every governed reference while preserving semantics serialization and external compatibility unless separately specified.
major_error_concepts: Running a textual replacement that changes unrelated concepts or externally stable names.
cards.prompt: Define Rename refactoring contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A rename refactoring updates the concept's identifier.
A rename refactoring updates every governed reference to that identifier.
A rename refactoring preserves program semantics unless a semantic change is separately specified.
A rename refactoring preserves serialization behavior unless a serialization change is separately specified.
A rename refactoring preserves external compatibility unless a compatibility change is separately specified.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The tradeoff of distributing variant behavior behind substitutable implementations only when variants are stable and contracts align.
major_error_concepts: Creating class hierarchies for short unstable conditionals and hiding the full behavior matrix.
cards.prompt: Define Replace-conditional-with-polymorphism boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The tradeoff of distributing variant behavior behind substitutable implementations only when variants are stable and contracts align.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The evidence that one conceptual change requires coordinated edits across many weakly owned locations and risks omission.
major_error_concepts: Calling any multi-file feature bad design even when separate interfaces legitimately need adaptation.
cards.prompt: Define Shotgun-change diagnostic. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The evidence that one conceptual change requires coordinated edits across many weakly owned locations and risks omission.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A small refactoring transformation is one behavior-preserving structural change narrow enough to review, validate, and revert independently.
major_error_concepts: Combining extraction renaming new behavior dependency upgrade and formatting into one untraceable step.
cards.prompt: Define Small refactoring transformation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A small refactoring transformation is one behavior-preserving structural change narrow enough to review, validate, and revert independently.

accepted_variants: It records an engineering condition, its cost/risk and remediation/ownership decision. It can arise unintentionally and be discovered later; deliberate acceptance is not required.
cards.definition: A technical-debt item records a design or implementation condition whose remediation cost and continuing development/operational burden warrant an explicit decision. Useful records identify the condition, impact, proposed remediation/principal, recurring interest/risk, ownership and disposition. Debt may be deliberate or inadvertent; discovery after learning more about the design does not invalidate the debt classification.
major_error_concepts: Only an intentionally chosen shortcut can be technical debt; an inadvertent design liability cannot qualify.
cards.prompt: What is a technical-debt item, and can debt be inadvertent rather than deliberately accepted?
required_concepts: Connect the item to a concrete engineering condition, remediation work and continuing cost/risk rather than personal dislike alone.
Allow deliberate and inadvertent origins.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The binding of approval to the exact reviewed commit set and policies for later mutation rather than to a branch or person indefinitely.
major_error_concepts: Treating approval as valid for all future commits in the same pull request.
cards.prompt: Define Approval content identity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The binding of approval to the exact reviewed commit set and policies for later mutation rather than to a branch or person indefinitely.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The mapping from each finding to agreement clarification changed artifact test or reasoned rejection with exact content identity.
major_error_concepts: Resolving threads through assertion or social agreement without changed-artifact readback.
cards.prompt: Define Author-response evidence. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The mapping from each finding to agreement clarification changed artifact test or reasoned rejection with exact content identity.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The dependence of safe change or recovery on knowledge held by too few available people or undocumented processes.
major_error_concepts: Counting names in a file while only one person has actual knowledge or access.
cards.prompt: Define Bus-factor risk. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The dependence of safe change or recovery on knowledge held by too few available people or undocumented processes.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The directed graph showing which review units require which accepted snapshots so stack order and parallelism are explicit.
major_error_concepts: Using numbered titles without exact base branches or dependency evidence.
cards.prompt: Define Change dependency graph. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The directed graph showing which review units require which accepted snapshots so stack order and parallelism are explicit.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The named responsibility for maintaining a surface reviewing consequential changes resolving residuals and preserving its contracts over time.
major_error_concepts: Using file authorship or a stale ownership pattern as proof of current responsibility.
cards.prompt: Define Code ownership contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The named responsibility for maintaining a surface reviewing consequential changes resolving residuals and preserving its contracts over time.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The single behavioral structural or evidential objective that makes all included modifications necessary to one review decision.
major_error_concepts: Treating all work from one ticket or week as one cohesive change.
cards.prompt: Define Cohesive change purpose. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The single behavioral structural or evidential objective that makes all included modifications necessary to one review decision.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The durable context alternatives decision consequences dissent owner status and supersession rule for a team-scale engineering choice.
major_error_concepts: Recording only the winning option or treating an old decision as timeless despite changed constraints.
cards.prompt: Define Collaborative decision record. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The durable context alternatives decision consequences dissent owner status and supersession rule for a team-scale engineering choice.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The judgment of whether code is harder to understand operate or change than the problem requires including control state abstraction and performance complexity.
major_error_concepts: Rejecting any abstraction as complex or accepting it because it is reusable.
cards.prompt: Define Complexity review dimension. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The judgment of whether code is harder to understand operate or change than the problem requires including control state abstraction and performance complexity.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The judgment of whether responsibilities interfaces dependencies data flow and alternatives fit the specified problem and future change boundary.
major_error_concepts: Deferring every design issue because code compiles or demanding a complete architecture redesign outside scope.
cards.prompt: Define Design review dimension. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The judgment of whether responsibilities interfaces dependencies data flow and alternatives fit the specified problem and future change boundary.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The context decisions current state exact artifacts validation known failures residuals owners and next actions enabling another maintainer to continue without guessing.
major_error_concepts: Sending a branch link and saying finish the tests.
cards.prompt: Define Engineering handoff package. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: An engineering handoff package states the relevant context.
An engineering handoff package records the decisions already made.
An engineering handoff package records the current system and work state.
An engineering handoff package identifies the exact artifacts under handoff.
An engineering handoff package records the validation already performed.
An engineering handoff package records known failures.
An engineering handoff package records residual risks or unresolved work.
An engineering handoff package names the responsible owners.
An engineering handoff package states the next actions.
Together, those fields let another maintainer continue without reconstructing essential facts by guesswork.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The trace from requested behavior through control data errors state changes and edge cases in the actual patch.
major_error_concepts: Reading only new tests or happy-path code and assuming they cover the implementation wiring.
cards.prompt: Define Functionality review dimension. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The trace from requested behavior through control data errors state changes and edge cases in the actual patch.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The coordinated judgment that names reveal domain intent comments explain nonobvious reasons style follows project rules and docs match consumer behavior.
major_error_concepts: Blocking on personal formatting already governed by automation while missing stale user documentation.
cards.prompt: Define Naming-comment-style-doc review. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The coordinated judgment that names reveal domain intent comments explain nonobvious reasons style follows project rules and docs match consumer behavior.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The reconciliation of every changed line generated file dependency and deletion against the declared purpose and preserved user work.
major_error_concepts: Reviewing only source files while generated outputs or configuration carry the actual behavior change.
cards.prompt: Define Patch-scope audit. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The reconciliation of every changed line generated file dependency and deletion against the declared purpose and preserved user work.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The author-provided problem approach alternatives behavior changes non-goals risks tests rollout screenshots or traces and exact review order.
major_error_concepts: Repeating the ticket title or narrating files without decisions and risks.
cards.prompt: Define Review description contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The author-provided problem approach alternatives behavior changes non-goals risks tests rollout screenshots or traces and exact review order.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The explicit distinction among blocking correctness or maintainability defects questions nonblocking suggestions and separately owned follow-ups.
major_error_concepts: Labeling all feedback comments equally so approval can hide unresolved material defects.
cards.prompt: Define Review finding classification. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The explicit distinction among blocking correctness or maintainability defects questions nonblocking suggestions and separately owned follow-ups.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The tradeoff among interruption cost queue time feedback size integration risk and ownership used to choose prompt bounded review units.
major_error_concepts: Optimizing only reviewer message count while cycle time and defect risk grow.
cards.prompt: Define Review latency and batching. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The tradeoff among interruption cost queue time feedback size integration risk and ownership used to choose prompt bounded review units.

accepted_variants: Commit one adds new_name with old_name forwarding compatibly and tests unchanged whitespace through both names. Commit two changes the declared whitespace contract with its own tests/docs. Revert the behavior step as allowed; before reverting the name bridge, remove or adapt later dependents.
cards.definition: First introduce new_name while keeping old_name as a compatible alias or forwarding wrapper, update governed internal references, and test that both entry points retain the old whitespace behavior. Second make the intentional whitespace change under an explicit approved compatibility policy and update tests/documentation for the promised behavior. Keep claims/evidence separate. Revert the behavior change independently when compatible; reverting the naming bridge may require reverting or adapting later dependents rather than blindly applying inverse changes.
major_error_concepts: Delete old_name and rename tests in commit one; green tests prove old callers still work, and either stacked commit can always be reverted independently.
cards.prompt: A proposal renames public function old_name to new_name and intentionally changes whitespace behavior. Existing callers of old_name must remain supported during the migration. Outline two coherent green commits, each claim/evidence, and a safe revert plan that accounts for dependencies.
required_concepts: Separate a compatibility-preserving naming bridge from the intentional whitespace behavior change.
Test both supported names at the first boundary and identify the second commit's changed contract/evidence.
Give a revert path that checks later name/behavior dependencies rather than assuming arbitrary independent reversion.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The inspection of whether tests exercise specified behavior decisive failures state effects independence and regression risk rather than merely exist.
major_error_concepts: Approving because coverage increased while the critical poststate is unasserted.
cards.prompt: Define Test review dimension. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The inspection of whether tests exercise specified behavior decisive failures state effects independence and regression risk rather than merely exist.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The directed relation among source generation compilation testing packaging and artifact nodes used to order work and invalidate stale outputs.
major_error_concepts: Treating the build script's textual order as proof all dependencies are declared.
cards.prompt: Define Build graph. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The directed relation among source generation compilation testing packaging and artifact nodes used to order work and invalidate stale outputs.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The distinction between using verified cached inputs to accelerate work and reusing stale outputs that no longer establish the current claim.
major_error_concepts: Calling any cache unsafe or any cache hit equivalent to a fresh execution.
cards.prompt: Define Cache-evidence boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The distinction between using verified cached inputs to accelerate work and reusing stale outputs that no longer establish the current claim.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The dependency and condition graph among build test lint package security and artifact jobs including skips cancellation and matrix dimensions.
major_error_concepts: Reading the visual green summary without checking skipped or nonrequired jobs.
cards.prompt: Define CI job graph. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The dependency and condition graph among build test lint package security and artifact jobs including skips cancellation and matrix dimensions.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The event branch path actor or manual dispatch and exact checkout identity that starts an automated evidence run.
major_error_concepts: Treating a green workflow name as current evidence for any branch state.
cards.prompt: Define Continuous-integration trigger. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The event branch path actor or manual dispatch and exact checkout identity that starts an automated evidence run.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A source file dependency tool configuration data generator or environment value intentionally included in the build relation.
major_error_concepts: Assuming only tracked source files influence the build.
cards.prompt: Define Declared build input. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A source file dependency tool configuration data generator or environment value intentionally included in the build relation.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The rules and identities selecting direct and transitive package versions sources integrity metadata and platform variants.
major_error_concepts: Reporting the manifest range as the exact dependency set or trusting names without hashes or sources.
cards.prompt: Define Dependency-resolution contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The rules and identities selecting direct and transitive package versions sources integrity metadata and platform variants.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The exact operating system architecture runtime toolchain locale timezone environment variables and relevant host constraints accompanying build or test evidence.
major_error_concepts: Saying works on my machine without enough identity to reproduce or bound the claim.
cards.prompt: Define Environment identity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Environment identity records the exact operating system accompanying build or test evidence.
Environment identity records the processor architecture.
Environment identity records the runtime version and identity.
Environment identity records the toolchain version and identity.
Environment identity records the locale.
Environment identity records the timezone.
Environment identity records the relevant environment variables without exposing secret values.
Environment identity records relevant host constraints.
The recorded environment is bound to the particular build or test evidence it qualifies.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The explicit denominator seed environment retry history owner and decision for a check whose result varies without governed input change.
major_error_concepts: Rerunning until pass and deleting prior results or permanently ignoring the test.
cards.prompt: Define Flaky-check disposition. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The explicit denominator seed environment retry history owner and decision for a check whose result varies without governed input change.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The degree to which the build obtains all governed inputs from declared isolated sources while acknowledging hardware kernel or toolchain residuals.
major_error_concepts: Calling container use complete reproducibility or rejecting practical isolation because no system is metaphysically closed.
cards.prompt: Define Hermetic-build boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The degree to which the build obtains all governed inputs from declared isolated sources while acknowledging hardware kernel or toolchain residuals.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The binding among version source commit tag build receipt artifact checksum signature provenance notes and promotion record whose versioned contents cannot be replaced.
major_error_concepts: Treating a tag or filename as sufficient identity while artifacts can be replaced.
cards.prompt: Define Immutable-release identity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Immutable-release identity binds the declared release version to a source commit.
Immutable-release identity binds the release to its tag.
Immutable-release identity binds the release to its build receipt.
Immutable-release identity binds the release to the checksum of the produced artifact.
Immutable-release identity records the artifact signature when a signature is part of the release contract.
Immutable-release identity records the release's provenance notes.
Immutable-release identity records the promotion decision and destination.
The contents associated with an already released version cannot be replaced in place.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The controlled comparison locating timestamp ordering locale randomness path compression parallelism or tool-version causes of hash divergence.
major_error_concepts: Normalizing the final hash or excluding the differing file without deciding whether it belongs.
cards.prompt: Define Nondeterministic-artifact diagnostic. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The controlled comparison locating timestamp ordering locale randomness path compression parallelism or tool-version causes of hash divergence.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The name version dependencies entry points compatibility license provenance and file inventory consumers receive with a distributable artifact.
major_error_concepts: Testing installed code while metadata points to the wrong version or omits required resources.
cards.prompt: Define Package metadata contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The name version dependencies entry points compatibility license provenance and file inventory consumers receive with a distributable artifact.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The property that independently executed builds from equivalent declared inputs produce bit-for-bit identical governed outputs under the release.
major_error_concepts: Calling deterministic behavior in one process proof that independent environments reproduce the artifact.
cards.prompt: Define Reproducible-build relation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The property that independently executed builds from equivalent declared inputs produce bit-for-bit identical governed outputs under the release.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The prepromotion evidence that identifies prior good artifact compatibility state effects operator steps validation and stop conditions for restoring service or source.
major_error_concepts: Writing rollback available with no tested artifact data or command path.
cards.prompt: Define Rollback-and-revert readiness. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Rollback-and-revert readiness identifies the prior known-good artifact or source state.
Rollback-and-revert readiness records compatibility requirements for returning to that state.
Rollback-and-revert readiness records the state effects that restoration may create or fail to reverse.
Rollback-and-revert readiness gives operators exact restoration steps.
Rollback-and-revert readiness specifies how the restored state will be validated.
Rollback-and-revert readiness defines stop conditions for abandoning or escalating the restoration.
The evidence states whether the planned operation restores deployed service, source history, or both.

accepted_variants: Keep credentials and private/symmetric keys in controlled secret storage and out of logs/source/build leakage. A public verification key can be shared; protect its authenticity and integrity, not secrecy merely because it is a key.
cards.definition: Passwords, bearer credentials, private keys, symmetric secret keys and other confidential values require authorized storage/access and controlled runtime delivery, and should not leak into source control, logs, public caches, test data or distributable builds. Public verification keys are designed to be shareable, although their authenticity/integrity must be protected. Authorized secret stores are not the same as accidental embedding or public exposure.
major_error_concepts: Every cryptographic key, including a public signature-verification key, must be treated as confidential and can never be distributed.
cards.prompt: Which credential and key material belongs behind a secret boundary? Are public verification keys secret merely because they are cryptographic keys? How does the protection of a public verification key differ?
required_concepts: Identify confidential credentials/private or symmetric keys as secrets needing controlled access/delivery and leakage prevention.
Distinguish public verification keys, which may be distributed but still require authentic trusted binding.

accepted_variants: Patch for compatible fixes only; minor for compatible API additions or marking a public feature deprecated; major for breaks, resetting lower components. 0.y.z is initial development, and prerelease labels precede their corresponding normal release.
cards.definition: Stable releases use a patch increment for only backward-compatible bug fixes, minor for new backward-compatible API functionality or newly marking public functionality deprecated, and major for incompatible API changes.
